industry.key: K. Professional, business and consumer services
industry.why: Neutral, carried; the sectors are split (Testing B, Recruitment D, the rest C) and carry the view. Relative strength B (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; C prior). Kepler (26-Nov) likes testing and inspection (Bureau Veritas, a private equity approach) and Hatzius (Goldman, 22-Nov) sees early signs of AI weighing on the job market, which is one sector up and one down. No change.

sector.why: Neutral, carried: the 'first budget cut' case has not appeared in the growth data (US GDP 4.3%), while advertising is still the first discretionary corporate cut when the margin rolls over; no source spoke to it. Relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; C prior). Pool names WPP, Publicis, JCDecaux. Balanced; Neutral by judgement.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No Swedish survey and no Riksbank reading reached the pack; the Swedish evidence is sector-level (Nordic small and mid caps de-rating, HMS Networks a buy after one of the largest multiple contractions in the Nordics, Swedish niche game publishers down 4%; Danske, 22 and 26-Nov), which the Fragility row carries. Four live holdings are Swedish (Avanza 5.30%, Elekta 3.98%, Hexatronic 4.89%, Sdiptech 5.76%; 19.93 points, 39% of invested weight), judged in component 5 and amendment 10. Relative strength is not graded by country.
